Four headless browsers each boot Quake II: the host loads demo1 as a listen server, then three joiners (server list, toast after a 20-second poll, a ?room= link) connect over WebRTC and load the level. 203 seconds at load 34; its own 540-second budget covers a slower box, plus 60 seconds for Chrome and cleanup.

Three emulator processes (server + two clients) on the virtual LAN: the clients' city is live only near batch 290000 at ~1000-1300 batches/s once joined, so they get a 420-second guard and the server 450; 540 seconds for the whole pair plus 60 for startup and cleanup. Heavy: run it on a boat sandbox.

Two Age of Empires II processes on the wall clock (--real-ticks), driven over their control channels: about 50 seconds of menus per seat, the guest started after the host has created its game, then a join and 15 seconds of lobby settling; about 150 seconds on a boat, so a 300-second guest guard per seat plus room for event waits, startup and cleanup. Heavy: run it on a boat sandbox.

Two Age of Empires processes on the wall clock (--real-ticks): each menu step waits for its screen to appear in a capture (the intro videos run their real length), the guest starts after the host has created its game, then a join and 15 seconds of lobby settling; about 2.5 minutes on a boat, so a 300-second guard per seat plus room for startup and cleanup. Heavy: run it on a boat sandbox.

Two Diablo processes on the virtual LAN at --tick-ms-per-batch=50 and 12-35 batches/s: the host reaches Tristram near batch 4300 (about five and a half minutes on a boat), then the guest joins at 10 ms a batch and downloads the game behind a progress bar (up to five minutes allowed); each seat has an 840-second guard, plus startup and cleanup. Heavy: run it on a boat sandbox.

Diablo II's Direct3D route to character creation and the Act I load costs 49 seconds of user CPU and about 55 seconds of wall clock on an idle box; its 420-second guest guard is sized for this machine at load 50, where the same work gets a fraction of a core, plus 60 seconds for loading and cleanup.
